Join us for the Data & AI Hackathon , an electrifying 8-hour sprint bringing together the brightest minds in data engineering, machine learning, and AI, all under one roof at the iconic AWS Builder Loft in San Francisco!
🚀 Whether you're an AI researcher, data scientist, backend engineer, or prompt designer, this is your chance to build next-generation intelligent systems, explore real-time data pipelines, and connect with the most passionate builders in the Bay Area.
🗓️ Event Details
When: 09:30 AM – 6:00 PM, September 11, 2026

Where: AWS Builder Loft, San Francisco, CA

Theme: Data & AI Infrastructure, Agentic Workflows & Foundation Models

High-Energy Building Sessions: 8 hours to prototype cutting-edge Data & AI solutions.

Data & AI Challenges: Solve real-world problems around intelligent automation, real-time analytics, vector search, and LLM orchestration.

Expert Mentorship: On-site guidance from veteran AI researchers and infrastructure engineers.

Swag, Catering & Networking: Fuel up with snacks and lunch while connecting with fellow builders and founders.

Prizes & Demos: Win exciting prizes and pitch your build directly to AI investors and industry leaders.

09:30 AM – 10:00 AM: Check-in & Breakfast ☕

10:00 AM – 11:00 AM: Keynote, Theme Briefing & API Workshops

11:00 AM – 12:00 PM: Hacking Starts & Team Formation

12:00 PM – 01:00 PM: Lunch Break 🍕🍽️

01:00 PM – 03:30 PM: Deep Hacking & Mentor Office Hours

04:40 PM – 05:00 PM: Awards & Closing Ceremony

05:00 PM – 06:00 PM: Networking & Happy Hour

🤝 About Our Partners
RocketRide
RocketRide is an open-source, developer-native AI meta-harness. Build, debug, and deploy production AI workflows right inside your IDE. And with RocketRide Cloud , teams can offload the complexity of AI infrastructure and focus on building solutions, with cost-efficient execution through our proprietary model server, shared pipelines for collaboration, higher performance, and seamless scalability.
🎁 Free credits: We're giving away free credits for RocketRide Cloud, 100% off your first purchase with a promo code. Join the Discord to grab yours.

📖 Step-by-step guide: Setup, demos, and how to build on RocketRide (Cloud + open-source): click here

🚀 Submit your project: Post it in the #showcase channel on Discord . Make sure to include your project’s GitHub link and all your .pipe files (import them from RocketRide Cloud). Need help? Just ask our bot in #support, whether it’s about your project or the tools.

Let's build something awesome together. 💻✨
RocketRide Rewards:
Two ways to win with RocketRide at Build Fast. Launch Loud.
🚀 Best Use of RocketRide: Build your project on RocketRide Cloud and deploy an AI pipeline without managing any infrastructure. Our hackathon app will track which team uses RocketRide the most, and the winning team takes home Apple AirPods Pro 3 worth $1,000! 🔥

New to RocketRide? Cloud is live: cloud.rocketride.ai 🚀
Snyk
Snyk is a developer-first cybersecurity platform that helps teams build fast without compromising on security. As developers rely heavily on AI to write code at unprecedented speeds, Snyk continuously scans and secures application code, open-source dependencies, containers, and cloud environments right within the developer’s workflow. For an AI hackathon, it matters because shipping code quickly with AI generators or autonomous agents also means shipping security risks at machine speed. Snyk acts as an intelligent security layer, catching vulnerabilities and automatically applying verified fixes in real time—allowing builders to ship ambitious AI projects safely and with complete confidence.
At this event you will learn:
1) Sign-up for free (no credit card required), how to import your code, and configure your AI coding tool
2) Free AI Security Engineer Foundations Certificate

About Event

Build It. Test It. Prove It.
Smells like a hackathon. Runs like a pressure test, on you, not just your idea.
Proving Ground runs a three-day Sprint where judges push past the pitch. No script survives real questions about what you tried, what broke, and what you changed.
Past teams have gone on to raise from 500 Global and Blitzscaling Ventures, and been accepted into Berkeley SkyDeck and Confluent's accelerator, independently, without Proving Ground's involvement in those decisions.
What this is
A hackathon judges what you built by the end. We watch during the process and look past the end to what may come next.

The team is almost everything. How you make decisions under pressure, how you handle a setback, how you treat each other when something breaks. You'll document that as you go. What we ask you to show and how we question it are built around behavior, not performance.
How it works
Over three days, founders build under real constraint. No script, no rehearsed demo. Judges probe what you tried, what broke, and what you changed, and compare where you started to where you ended.
Two Tracks
Discovery Track. Pre-market, no active customer contact yet. For the startup curious, including enterprise folks seriously exploring a leap.
Pre-seed Track. In-market, already talking to customers. Ship something real, show what's changed, pressure-test your next move.
After the Sprint
Select teams get invited into the Street Test: 30 days back in the real world, no artificial deadline, no audience. This is where we see if momentum was real or borrowed from the room. It's the part a hackathon can't offer, because a hackathon ends when the weekend does.

Every era has one question it can’t stop asking.

What happens when intelligence stops being scarce?

06 · Rethinking What We Build — The Next Decade of Building Starts Here
https://loomus.ai/series
Episode 01 asked how AI is changing the way we discover information.
Episode 02 asks what happens when AI starts doing the work.
For decades, software has waited for humans to tell it what to do.
Open the app.
Click the button.
Write the prompt.
Execute the task.
AI agents are beginning to change that relationship.
Instead of simply responding to instructions, increasingly capable AI systems can reason, plan, use tools, maintain context, coordinate across systems, and take actions toward a goal.
We are beginning to move from:
Tools → Collaborators
Tasks → Outcomes
Software → Autonomous Systems
And that shift could reshape much more than productivity.
It could change how companies are built, how teams operate, how software is designed, how organizations allocate work, and ultimately what it means to work alongside machines.
We are moving from an era where humans operate software to one where humans increasingly delegate to intelligence .
Join us at Stanford for Episode 02 of Rethinking the World in the Age of AI , as we bring together builders, researchers, founders, investors, and operators to explore the rapidly emerging world of AI agents — and what it means for the next decade of work.

Cheryl Cheng
Managing Partner, M12 — Microsoft’s Venture Fund

She brings more than 16 years of experience investing in companies from early to growth stages. Before joining M12, Cheryl founded and led Vive Collective, a healthcare investment platform, and served as a General Partner at BlueRun Ventures. She holds a B.A. in Public Policy from Stanford University and an MBA from Northwestern University’s Kellogg School of Management. Cheryl also advises Stanford Biodesign and works closely with the Stanford d.school .
Laura Lin
Head of Growth & Community, Collov AI
Laura Lin is the Head of Growth & Community at Collov AI, an AI-powered interior design platform transforming how consumers and businesses approach the design process. She leads growth and community initiatives, helping expand Collov AI’s presence and engagement across the AI and design ecosystem. Prior to Collov AI, Laura gained experience at Google and Meta, bringing a strong background in technology, growth, and community building. She is also an active contributor to the AI startup community, frequently participating in conversations around AI agents, consumer technology, and the practical adoption of generative AI.

A mathematician and AI researcher trained at Télécom Paris and Imperial College London, Yann specializes in neuro-symbolic AI, world-model agents, and graph-based reasoning. At Rippletide, he leads the development of its decision context graph technology, which combines structured knowledge and symbolic reasoning to make AI-agent decisions more reliable, explainable, and auditable. His work focuses on building the infrastructure needed for autonomous agents to operate safely in complex enterprise environments. In 2026, Yann also won the OpenAI Codex Hackathon with a multi-agent system for autonomous scientific discovery.

She has also founded and developed AI-powered learning and content products, including DouXing and ChatSlide.AI. A Stanford alumna, Sophie has been recognized by Forbes 30 Under 30 and Hurun 30 Under 30, and remains actively involved in the Stanford entrepreneurial community, supporting founders and emerging technologies across AI and education.

About Event

For three years, using AI meant typing into a box and waiting for text to come back.
That era is ending.

The next interface isn't a chat window. It's worn, spoken, and always on.
Glasses that listen.
A pendant that remembers.
A tracker you never charge.
A second self that watches your screen and acts before you ask.
We're putting the founders building that future in one room with the people who want to build on it.

Half a day in San Francisco.

Real hardware on the table. Working demos, not slideware.
The lineup is a short list of founders shipping the wearables that are pulling AI off the screen.

The founders in the room:
Adam Cohen Hillel, Secondly - a personal AI "second self" that sees your screen and acts across every app you use. The chat box becomes a presence.

Nik Shevchenko, Omi - the open-source AI wearable necklace, with 250+ developer apps already built on it. Always listening, always yours.

AnhPhu Nguyen, Mira - AI smart glasses with no camera. They hear what you hear, recall every name, and translate 60+ languages in under a second. AnhPhu is the Harvard builder behind last year's viral I-XRAY demo.

Andy Kong, Chargerless - a 7-gram health tracker powered by daylight. One minute of sun a day and it never needs a charger.

What you'll build: pick a device, an API, or a live sensor stream.

Ship something a person could actually wear or talk to by the time we demo.

The strongest builds demo to the founders in the room.
This is for builders, hardware hackers, AI engineers, and designers who think the keyboard is a temporary technology.
